lab_overview.institution: Northbridge University — School of Pharmacy & Biomedical Sciences
description: The Advanced Drug Delivery Laboratory investigates how nanoscale drug-delivery systems can improve the delivery of therapeutic molecules to cells and tissues
The lab develops and characterises nanoparticle-based delivery systems, with particular interests in improving therapeutic stability, cellular uptake and targeted delivery

Its work combines formulation development, physicochemical characterisation, imaging and cell-based evaluation to understand how the properties of drug-delivery systems influence their biological performance

principal_investigator.name: Professor Maya Shah
research_interests: Relationships between nanoparticle properties and biological performance
research_focus: Professor Shah's research focuses on understanding how drug-delivery systems can be designed and optimised to improve the transport of therapeutic molecules into target cells

Her group combines formulation development with physical characterisation and biological testing to understand how characteristics such as particle size, dispersity and encapsulation influence delivery performance

core_research_themes.purpose: These measurements help researchers understand why apparently similar formulations may behave differently biologically

projects.title: Optimising lipid nanoparticles for nucleic-acid delivery
description: The lab investigated how changes in lipid nanoparticle composition affected particle characteristics and transfection performance.
Different formulations were produced and compared based on particle size, dispersity, encapsulation and their ability to deliver nucleic acids in cultured cells.
The project identified formulation characteristics associated with improved delivery performance and generated candidate formulations for further investigation.

projects.title: Understanding nanoparticle structure and formulation stability
description: The group investigated how the internal structure of nanoparticle formulations changed under different formulation and storage conditions
Particle characterisation was combined with electron microscopy and neutron-scattering measurements accessed through a collaborating research facility
The project sought to connect structural changes with formulation stability and performance

projects.title: Imaging cellular uptake of nanoparticle delivery systems
description: The lab investigated differences in cellular uptake between several experimental nanoparticle formulations

Imaging and quantitative image analysis were used alongside physicochemical measurements to examine whether differences in nanoparticle characteristics were associated with differences in cellular uptake
The work contributed to the lab's broader research into relationships between formulation properties and biological performance
